subject: POC availability: beltway & sunrise slots for global deep-dive

messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Liu <sandra.liu@acme-corp.com>, Devon Park <devon@edgewave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC availability: beltway & sunrise slots for global deep-dive

Hi Sandra / Devon —

Thanks again for agreeing to the hands-on POC. To make the technical deep-dive useful for your infra and app teams, we want to align on: prompt review, routing behavior, and a short load-test run covering your realistic traffic mix.

Quick ask: what are the team's availability constraints across your US / EU / APAC contributors? Instead of a single late-night slot for one region, we propose two short windows (we're calling them "beltway" and "sunrise") that rotate so no one is repeatedly outside working hours.

Attached: poc-agenda-v1.pdf and a timezone-matrix.csv I put together with preliminary slot ideas. My initial proposal:
- Beltway slot (US evening / EU morning): 17:00–18:30 PDT / 00:00–01:30 CEST
- Sunrise slot (US morning / APAC evening): 07:30–09:00 PDT / 22:30–00:00 AEST

Goals for the first session (90m):
- 20m prompt/case review (bring 2 example prompts each)
- 40m hands-on routing walkthrough + model variant failover
- 30m small-scale load test (bursting, KV cache warm-up, and autoscaler observability)

Can you confirm which (if either) of those windows works for your teams next week? If neither, share your constraints and we can propose an alternate rotation. We can also run the load test in a separate 45m slot if you prefer to keep the deep-dive focused on prompts/routing.

Thanks — I tried to keep it short. Attaching a lightweight agenda and the timezone matrix. Once we have a preferred window I’ll send a tentative calendar invite with the runbook link.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
attachments: poc-agenda-v1.pdf (application/pdf), timezone-matrix.csv (text/csv)
From: Sandra Liu <sandra.liu@acme-corp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 00:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: POC availability: beltway & sunrise slots for global deep-dive

Thanks, Stephanie. Helpful framing — appreciate the rotation idea. A couple of constraints from my side:
- Our EU infra folks (Paris/Berlin) prefer not to meet later than 17:30 CEST.
- APAC will join but only during APAC evening (we have product folks in SGP/AUS).
- We have a short blackout for on-call between 23–00 UTC next Tue.

Quick responses:
- The beltway slot as written will push EU too late; could we shift beltway earlier by 60 minutes on EU side?
- Sunrise slot looks okay for APAC but it’s rough for some US stakeholders.

If it helps, I can ask Devon to plot ideal times from EdgeWave's side (they'll be running the load profile). We want the deep-dive to include the routing policy changes you mentioned and a 25m load ramp to see autoscaler behavior.

Can you propose two concrete date/time options (one that favors EU and one that favors APAC) and we’ll pick.

—Sandra
Sandra Liu
Infrastructure Lead, Acme Corp
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 22 Jun 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC availability: beltway & sunrise slots for global deep-dive

Looping in operational details and two concrete options as Sandra asked. I recommended keeping sessions <=90m and splitting load-run into a separate 45m if there are timezone pain points. Proposed slots (we've adjusted beltway earlier by 60m on EU):

Option A – EU-favored (best for Paris/Berlin):
- Mon 28 Jun 2027 16:00–17:30 CEST / Sun 27 Jun 2027 07:00–08:30 PDT (Beltway-early)
- Follow-up load run: Tue 29 Jun 2027 09:00–09:45 CEST (separate 45m window)

Option B – APAC-favored (best for SGP/AUS):
- Wed 30 Jun 2027 22:30–00:00 AEST / Wed 30 Jun 2027 07:30–09:00 PDT (Sunrise)
- Follow-up load run: Thu 01 Jul 2027 09:30–10:15 AEST (separate 45m)

Operational notes:
- We'll pre-stage a model variant with quantized weights for the load run to limit GPU memory churn.
- Devon, if you can share the 95th-percentile request distribution you'll run, we can tailor the autoscaler ramp.
- I'll attach a short runbook and the timezone-matrix.csv with participant names mapped to slots.

If either option works for Acme, I can send the calendar invites and include the runbook + Doc link. If both are tough, we'll propose a rotating cadence where the first session follows Option A and the second rotates to Option B, so no single region always takes the late or early slot.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
attachments: runbook-brief.md, timezone-matrix.csv
